Hi Andrew — thanks for the context and the quick summary. Short answer: yes. Attached below is a concise proposal and a few negotiation levers we typically use (burst credits, carryover, SLA anchors, and phased glidepaths).

High-level commit ladder (annual, pre-paid token commits):
- Starter: 250M tokens/year — list price $0.00015/token, committed price $0.00012/token
- Growth: 1.2B tokens/year — committed price $0.000095/token (5% overage at committed rate)
- Enterprise: 6B tokens/year — committed price $0.000075/token, includes prioritized routing and 2% rollback credit for missed SLA

Burst credits: one-time pool of burst tokens (50–200% of monthly run-rate depending on tier) that can be consumed at committed rates for spikes. Carryover: unused committed tokens can carry up to 15% to the next month, or consolidated at quarter.

SLA anchors: we can contract an availability SLA (99.9% for Growth, 99.95%+ for Enterprise) and commit to latency p95 targets for model sizes you run; failure to meet targets triggers credits that flow back to invoice.

I've attached a short PDF with example math and a proposed mutual action plan. /karthik

Attachments: redwood_commit_proposal_v2.pdf

Regards,

Subject: internal: Helios — SLA anchors and discount glidepath

Karthik — quick internal note before you send: a couple of negotiation points that helped close similar deals last quarter.

1) Glidepath discounts: start at midpoint committed price for Q1 (e.g., Growth: $0.00011/token) and step down to full committed pricing by Q3 when usage is validated. This reduces client friction on commit size.
2) Burst credit sizing: offer 1.5x monthly burst for Growth, 2x for Enterprise. Make burst consumption first-in-line before overage billing.
3) Exec SLA anchor: for Enterprise, add a one-time onboarding credit if p95 latency target isn't met in the first 45 days — it's a cheap confidence signal.

Ben, want me to draft the revised wording for the proposal PDF?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
